results.title: Large language models in climate and sustainability policy
results.content: # Large language models in climate and sustainability policy: limits and opportunities. We apply general and domain-specific large language models (LLMs) to two case studies and we document appropriate uses and shortcomings of these tools for two tasks: classification and sentiment analysis of climate and sustainability documents. In this work, we provide an empirical and critical overview of the use of LLMs for climate and sustainability policy purposes by investigating the process of two widely used tasks: text classification and sentiment analysis. Beyond data collection, data processing (figure 4, Step 2) poses the second challenge in applying automated routines (and particularly LLMs) to sustainability and climate policy documents. In the sustainability and climate policy domains, we acknowledge two additional risks identifiable in the model selection and output evaluation stages (figure 4, Step 3). Prompts in sustainability and climate policy may need refinement over several iterations and they may involve multiple experts in domain-specific knowledge compartments.
